news_list.title: Revival 0.4.0
news_list.short_description: Quest fixes (the candles, Thorstein, the mushrooms, the Intruder's endings), oils at full strength, smoother fights, fairer shop prices and packs that show what was inside.
news_list.content:
What changed in 0.4.0:

SHOP
- New prices for casual play (the Revival preset): potions, oils and bombs cost a half to two thirds of what they did, bait 150 gold coins, ingredients and crafting stations about 40% less, swords and armor a quarter less, and bags half.
- Daily deals are 40% off (25% before).
- Chests are always a bargain: each costs about a quarter less than what is inside. A little something costs 90 gold coins, For professionals 280.
- Two new chests: Scrolls and bombs (2 Lesser Summoning Scrolls, 3 Grapeshot and 3 Dancing Star) and Set of bait (one of each bait).
- Every price is on the Rewards page of the dashboard. The Vanilla preset keeps the original prices.

PACKS
- A Herbalist's pack holds more: three finds, roots most often, also herbs and powdered monster tissue, and now and then monster remains.
- Opening packs in the inventory shows what was inside, one item at a time.
- A pack from a friend shows its rarest find, and the rest goes into your inventory with it.
- What a pack holds is on the Rewards page of the dashboard. In the Vanilla preset it holds herbs or roots, as its description says.
- Opening your last pack takes you back to the inventory (its window no longer comes back offering Open).

QUESTS
- The Sins of Our Fathers: each candle now burns out after its 15 minutes and the next one can be lit, so the curse can be lifted.
- Thorstein's Conversation button now starts his part in The Sins of Our Fathers and in Intruder.
- The Great Mushrooming: the mushrooms show even while another quest is tracked, one after every 100 m walked (200 m in the original game).
- Intruder: every ending can now be reached; deal with the frightener before the sorcerer's 24 hours are up for the best reward. Its 24-hour wait now ends as it should.
- Quest places are chosen by walking distance too: at most 1.5 km along the paths, so none waits across a river with no bridge.
- The Dark Side of the Full Moon: after the quest the blacksmith keeps his forge where you met him (Lothar if you spared him, the new smith if not), and sharpens your sword.
- Quest places stay put: they no longer move when you are far away or after the server restarts.
- Evil Never Sleeps: the Cursebreaker trinket now comes whichever way the amulet was thrown; if you finished the quest without it, it arrives on your next start.
- What Lurks in the Nemeta is offered once nemeta open (level 10), since it is played in one.

MONSTERS
- More monsters: 24 on a map cell instead of 18, with 32 places a cell to stand on.
- Fewer rares: about one monster in ten instead of one in six.
- Harder monsters come later: one skull from level 5, two from level 10, three (the legendaries) from level 15.
- Monsters and herbs no longer stand on top of quest markers.
- All of these are settings on the dashboard's Tuning and World pages.
- Monsters, herbs and quests stand off footpaths and streets (12 m beside a path, a Tuning setting).
- You can reach places on the map from 100 m away (67.5 m in the original game; a Tuning setting).
- Nemeta no longer stand on quest markers, and monsters that come back while you play keep clear of the markers too.

COMBAT
- Oils now give their full bonus: a 33% oil makes a blow 33% stronger, on top of weaknesses, potions and skills. The Vanilla preset keeps the original sum, and the oils' descriptions say so.
- Perfect parries pay their experience again once Hit Reflection is learnt.
- A level-up window that was missed (the game closed, the connection dropped) now shows after the next start.
- Potions and oils last 30 minutes (a Tuning setting): every fight in that time has them, and the effects panel on the map shows the time left. As many potions as your slots (a new one replaces the oldest) and one oil.
- Every monster you defeat drops gold coins: the rarer and harder, the more (3 to 38), and the fight's summary shows them. A nemeton pays its monsters' coins on top of its bounty. The amounts are on the Rewards page of the dashboard; the Vanilla preset pays none.
- Skills can be reset: in the skill tree, open any learned skill and tap Reset skills twice to get every point back.
- The blacksmith's sharpening now really works: +10% melee damage for an hour. And once you have Hit Reflection, deflected blows count as parries for Swordmaster and On Your Guard.
- Quen now protects you: its shield takes the whole blow that breaks it (it let every blow through before). The share is a Tuning setting; the Vanilla preset keeps the 70% players remember.
- Under Quen you can still try a perfect parry: if it lands, the blow is parried and the shield stays up.
- Reset skills now gives the points back at once, without reopening the game.
- Perfect parries count for Swordmaster and On Your Guard (a Tuning setting).

SMOOTHER PLAY
- Fights and encounters start at once: they no longer wait behind the map's slower requests.
- Less work for the phone while you play: the game's most frequent calls skip the hook's script, and inland map tiles are drawn faster.
- Your witcher walks smoothly on the map again: the hook's work that ran every frame now stays out of the way.

DASHBOARD AND APP
- Players: choose your character's gender and head; the game shows it at its next start.
- Tuning: new settings for oils, deflected blows, the walking between mushrooms, finds of untracked quests and the Intruder's endings, each with its original value in the Vanilla preset.
- Tuning: more of the game's own numbers are settings: from which level nemeta open and how many a day pay gold, the experience for perfect parries, perfect attacks, new monsters and the right oil, skill points per level and per bestiary tier, the skills' strengths, brewing time and how often a herbalist's pack drops. Those the game reads at its start apply once the server and the game start again.
- Guided setup: the game files now come from the Revival download (the Internet Archive), unchanged and checked, with no Google account. Had the game on your account before? Google Play through Aurora stays an option.
- Save Data: a restore checks the file first and leaves your progress as it was if anything is wrong. Stop the server before restoring.

GOOD TO KNOW
- This update changes the game itself: tap Update the game in the companion app.
- New prices apply once the server and the game start again.
- If you set monsters per cell or the rarity weights on the World page before, your own numbers stay: change them there.

Weather data by Open-Meteo.com. Map data from OpenStreetMap contributors. Questions and reports: join our Discord from the companion app.
